Neelam Sharma vs S K Sharma And Anr on 27 April, 2024 
 In The Court Of Sh. Sushil Kumar,
 Additional Sessions Judge-04,
 North District, Rohini Courts, Delhi. 
 Cnr No. Dlnt01-009163-2022
 Criminal Appeal No. 161/2022 
 Ps Prashant Vihar
Neelam Sharma
D/o Sh. V. D. Sharma,
R/o C-6/91, Sector-15, Rohini,
Delhi-110089. .....Appellant
 Vs.
1. S K Sharma
S/o Late Sh. Chavi Nath Sharma,
R/o: G-345, Gali No.17, West Karawal Nagar,
Delhi.
2. State
Through App, Department of Prosecution,
North-District, Rohini Courtgs, Delhi. 
 .....Respondent
Date of institution of appeal : 11.10.2022
Date on which judgment pronounced : 27.04.2024
 Judgment 
1. Vide this judgment, this Court shall dispose of the present appeal filed by appellant Neelam Sharma, under section 372 Cr.P.C. 1973, against judgment of acquittal dated 24.05.2022 (hereinafter referred to as impugned judgment) passed by the Court of Ld. MM-01, North- District,
Rohini Courts, Delhi (hereinafter referred to as Ld. Trial Court) in case bearing FIR No.100/2007,
PS Prashant Vihar, U/s. 406/498A/34 Neelam Sharma Vs. S K Sharma & Anr.
IPC in case titled as 'State Vs. Anurag Sharma' wherein prayer for setting-aside the impugned judgment of acquittal dated 24.05.2022 has been made. 
2. Being aggrieved by the impugned Judgment and Order on Sentence, the appellant has moved the present appeal on the following grounds :-
(i) That the judgment of acquittal dated 24.05.2022 is erroneous, bad in law and wrong on the facts and is liable to be set-aside (ii) Because the Ld. Trial Court has failed to appreciate that the prosecution has proved its case beyond reasonable doubt. That the Ld. Trial Court failed to appreciate Neelam Sharma vs S K Sharma And Anr on 27 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61024999/
1 that the appellant is a victim of mental and physical cruelty meted out to her by her husband and in-laws especially father-in-law. That the appellant's physical and mental health and safety have been in constant jeopardy since the beginning of her marriage. That the appellant's husband, father-in-law, mother-in-law and brother-in-law have been a constant threat to the life, liberty and safety of the appellant. That they have since the beginning of the appellant with Anurag Sharma tormented and harassed the appellant with the sole intent of coercing the appellant and her father into meeting their unlawful demands for money. 
Neelam Sharma Vs. S K Sharma & Anr. 
(iii) Because the Ld. Trial Court failed to acknowledge that since the very beginning of the marriage,
the appellant/aggrieved was harassed, humiliated and tortured by her husband, Respondent No.1,
by her mother-in-law and brother-in-law. That since the very beginning of the appellant's marriage,
respondent no.1 was not satisfied with the dowry given to them because it was insufficient in his estimation and thus, he started taunting and harassing the appellant. That, moreover, the Ld. Trial Court also failed to appreciate that during her stay in the marital home, the appellant experienced extreme brutality at the hands of her husband and her in-laws. 
(iv) Because the Ld. Trial Court failed to appreciate that the appellant's husband, respondent no.1,
her mother-in-law and brother-in-law unceremoniously kicked her out of her marital residence around six months into the union, and when she returned at their request under the assurance that she would not be tormented, respondent no.1 and the appellant's husband started hurling one obscenity laced tirade after another at the appellant. That, respondent no.1 further pressured the appellant into approaching her father for the purpose of the repayment of the loan taken by her husband prior to their marriage. In response, the appellant pleaded with respondent no.1 and said that her father had taken out a loan specifically for the purpose of her marriager and would therefore be unable to secure any additional cash for Neelam Sharma Vs. S K Sharma & Anr.
the repayment of the loan her husband had taken out. That despite the pleas of the appellant,
respondent no.1 got in touch with the appellant's father and demanded that he pay back the debt that his son-in-law had take out. However, the appellant's father refused to accede to his demand and out rightly said no. 
(v) That the Ld. Trial Court failed to acknowledge that in the light of the appellant's father having refused to pay back the said loan, the taunts and harassment by the husband, respondent no.1, her mother-in-law and brother-in-law increased many folds and they resorted to harassing, humiliating and beating the appellant on one pretext or the other and made the life of the appellant a living hell. 
That given the cruel conduct, appellant started remaining depressed and her condition started deteriorating day- by-day, which was further exacerbated by the fact that she was not ever provided with sufficient food in the matrimonial house. That the appellant's father-in-law threatened her that she would continue to experience repeated assaults and torment unless their dowry demands were satisfied. 
Neelam Sharma vs S K Sharma And Anr on 27 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61024999/
2 (vi) That the Ld. Trial Court has failed to appreciate that during the appellant's pregnancy, her in-laws instead of being happy and blessing her, continued to beat her and taunt her. That respondent no.1 and his wife, who were unhappy about the birth of a female child, neglected the health of the mother and the newborn girl Neelam Sharma Vs. S K Sharma & Anr.
child and continued to mete out horrible treatment of the appellant. That within one day of the delivery of the child, respondent no.1 and his wife, without providing any medical and post-delivery care, ordered that the appellant to continue with her daily chores. The appellant, despite being in a sensitive in a sensitive condition, performed all the households chores for the next eight days before her body succumbed, while the in-laws continue to torment her. Thus, she took the newborn baby daughter and fled to her maternal house in order to preserve both their lives. 
(vii) Because the Ld. Trial Court has failed to appreciate that the brother-in-law of the appellant is guilty of molesting and sexually harassing her and the fact that whenever the appellant complained about the same to her husband, he paid no heed to her words. That the appellant had to beg to her husband to move to a separate household. That, furthermore, respondent no.1 and his wife further harass the appellant, refused to return her jewelery and the other stridhan and dowry materials. 
Also, all the household furniture and utensils for the new household were provided by the Appellant's father. 
(viii) Because the Ld. Trial Court failed to appreciate that the respondent no.1 had during the delivery of the second child of the Neelam Sharma Vs. S K Sharma & Anr.
appellant visited her at her then residence at Rohini, merely to forcefully take all her jewelery. 
(ix) Because the Ld. Trial Court failed to appreciate that the appellant's husband, without the consent and permission of the appellant, the husband prematurely withdrew the Fixed Deposit that the appellant's father had created in favour of the appellant. That respondent no.1 and the appellant's father also sold the motorcycle that the appellant's father had given to Appellant's husband as dowry for their own delight. Furthermore, they forged the signatures of the appellant and in her name purchased a new motorcycle on EMI. In addition to the above, for their own gain and selfish motives, they further mortgaged the appellant's jewelery. They also made the appellant sign blank cheques under duress. 
(x) Because the Ld. Trial Court failed to acknowledge that since the motorcycle was purchased in the name of the appellant, she started receiving notices from the Bank on account of non- payment of installments. Having no other option, the loan installments were paid by the appellant's father in order to protect his daughter. That the appellant's father also discharged other loans and financial liabilities incurred by the Anurag Sharma and respondent no.1. That on being questioned by the Appellant's father, respondent no.1 argued that since the appellant had neither Neelam Sharma Vs.
S K Sharma & Anr.
brought dowry nor any property, thus, he (appellant's father) would have to discharge all their financial liabilities and pay for day-to-day expenses. 
Neelam Sharma vs S K Sharma And Anr on 27 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61024999/
3 (xi) Because the Ld. Trial Court failed to acknowledge that the appellant's husband fell into the company of immoral persons, who at times visited their house. That, it was during these visits that these persons used to also molest and sexually harass the appellant. That despite the appellant's frequent complaints and protests, the appellant's husband used to not only turned a blind eye towards the conduct of his friends, but would also beat the appellant and take any money her father gave her for gambling and drinking. His actions were abetted by respondent no.1. 
xii) Because the Ld. Trial Court failed to acknowledge that on one occasion, the appellant's husband had beaten her because of which she left her house and stayed at Kali Mandir, her father came to pick up her, when her father inquired from respondent no.1 about the same, respondent no.1 remarked that the appellant must be indulging in prostitution activity. In order to further afflict the appellant, respondent no.1 used to take away both his grandchildren with himself. Respondent no.1 also took away all the remaining jewellery of the complainant from her house. 
Neelam Sharma Vs. S K Sharma & Anr. 
3. It has been argued on behalf of appellant that impugned judgment dated 24.05.2022 passed by the Ld. Trial Court is illegal and incorrect and, therefore, the impugned judgment dated 24.05.2022 passed by the Ld. Trial Court may kindly be set-aside.
4. On the other hand, Ld. Counsel for respondent no.1 as well as Ld. Additional PP for State/
Respondent no.2 have strongly opposed the contentions made by Ld. Counsel for appellant and submits that the impugned order has been passed by Ld. Trial Court after considering the testimonies of Prosecution Witnesses and that the same has not been passed arbitrarily. Both of them have opposed the present appeal vehemently and they have prayed that the present appeal may kindly be dismissed. 
5. This Court has given thoughtful consideration to the arguments advanced on behalf of ld. Counsel for the appellant/accused as well as Ld. APP for State/Respondent. This Court has also perused the record. 
6. Perusal of the Trial Court Record shows that charge-sheet for the offences punishable under section 406/498A/34 IPC was filed in the Ld. Trial Court on 26.09.2008 against respondent no.1 S K Sharma and other persons. Perusal of the Trial Court Record further shows that vide order dated 23.03.2012, charge for the offence punishable under section 498A/34 IPC only was framed against respondent no.1 S K Sharma to which he had pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. It is pertinent to Neelam Sharma Vs. S K Sharma & Anr.
mention that the charge for the offence punishable under section 406/498A/34 IPC was also framed against another accused namely Anurag Sharma who was later on declared absconder in the afore- mentioned FIR case. 
7. Perusal of the Trial Court Record further shows that in order to prove its case, the prosecution examined as many as Three (03) prosecution witnesses and after closing of prosecution evidence,
Neelam Sharma vs S K Sharma And Anr on 27 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61024999/
4 the respondent no.1 S K Sharma was examined under Section 313 Criminal Procedure Code,
wherein he pleaded false implication and innocence. Perusal of the Trial Court Record further shows that respondent no.1 S K Sharma did not wish to lead defence evidence and therefore DE was closed and final arguments were heard. Perusal of the Trial Court Record further shows that vide impugned judgment dated 24.05.2022, Ld. Trial Court acquitted respondent no.1 S K Sharma for the offence punishable under Section 498A/34 IPC.
8. In the present case, Ld. Trial Court has appreciated and analyzed the testimonies of prosecution witnesses only qua respondent no.1 / accused S K Sharma for the charge of offence punishable under section 498A IPC framed against him as the co-accused Anurag Sharma was declared absconder vide order dated 12.11.2018. Ld. Trial Court has rightly given observation that mere demand of money or property unaccompanied by any harassment does not fall within the mischief of section 498A IPC and the allegations against respondent no.1 S K Neelam Sharma Vs. S K Sharma & Anr.
Sharma are not sufficient enough to prove his guilt for the offence punishable under section 498A IPC. Further, Ld. Trial Court has rightly observed that no specific date, month or year for demand of Rs.50,000/- has been mentioned and the even the date on which complainant was allegedly beaten by accused has not been mentioned either in the complaint or in testimony of complainant. Further,
there is no MLC of the complainant on record. 
9. Perusal of the Trial Court Record further shows that there are allegations against respondent no.1 S K Sharma that he rebuked the complainant by complainant that she should not have produce the children if she or her parents could not pay for her education which are rightly found to be vague by Ld. Trial Court in the impugned judgment dated 24.05.2022. The allegations that accused took both the daughters of complainant are also vague as neither any specific date or month of the said incident has been mentioned nor the daughters of the complainant have been examined before Ld.
Trial Court . Ld. Trial Court has rightly observed that the entire testimony of complainant shows that only allegation of dowry demand against respondent no.1 S K Sharma is demand of Rs.50,000/-
which is found to be vague and unsubstantiated and the remaining allegations against him are more in the nature of ordinary quarrels and wear and tear of matrimonial life. Ld. Trial Court has rightly observed that prosecution had failed to prove this case beyond reasonable doubts against respondent no.1 S K Sharma for the charge framed against him for the offence punishable under section Neelam Sharma Vs. S K Sharma & Anr.
498A IPC. Therefore, this Court is of view that judgment passed by Ld. Trial Court is well reasoned and a detailed judgment. 
10. In view of the above discussion, this Court is of considered view that the present appeal has been filed without any merit and same is liable to be dismissed. Same is dismissed accordingly. The judgment passed by Ld. Trial Court is accordingly, upheld. 
11. Let the Trial Court Record be sent back alongwith a copy of this order to Ld. Trial Court. 
Neelam Sharma vs S K Sharma And Anr on 27 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61024999/
5 12. Appeal file be consigned to Record Room after due compliance. 
13. A copy of this order be given to both the parties at free of cost. 
Pronounced in open Court on this 27th day of April, 2024. 
(SUSHIL KUMAR) Additional Sessions Judge-04 North: Rohini Courts: Delhi. 
27.04.2024 Neelam Sharma Vs. S K Sharma & Anr.

summary.arguments:

(i) That the judgment of acquittal dated 24.05.2022 is erroneous, bad in law and wrong on the facts and is liable to be set-aside (ii) Because the Ld. Trial Court has failed to appreciate that the prosecution has proved its case beyond reasonable doubt.
On the other hand, Ld. Counsel for respondent no.1 as well as Ld. Additional PP for State/
Respondent no.2 have strongly opposed the contentions made by Ld. Counsel for appellant and submits that the impugned order has been passed by Ld. Trial Court after considering the testimonies of Prosecution Witnesses and that the same has not been passed arbitrarily.
Both of them have opposed the present appeal vehemently and they have prayed that the present appeal may kindly be dismissed.
